Figure 2:Overview of SOLVE.At each call, the multimodal LLM agent queries a few pixels, which return depth through epipolar matching across cameras or monocular depth estimation, and writes an ordered sequence of several absolute keyposes that an executor follows along straight lines.
Offline, the agent reflects on its own rollouts, and the lessons are merged into general rules for self-improvement.

Figure 4:Three settings, three robots, one agent.RoboDojo-Sim tests precision, long horizons and memory with two ARX-X5 arms, RoboLab tests unseen objects and instructions on a single Franka without demonstrations, and the real UR12e robot tests transfer to hardware on 16 unseen tasks.
The same agent, tools and executor run in all three, with only the robot’s constants changed.
Figure 9:Real-robot episodes (1/2):Long-Horizon, Precision, Memory and the first Open tasks. Six third-person keyframes per episode, with the time since its start.
Figure 10:Real-robot episodes (2/2):the remaining Open tasks, in-context rebuilding, Gomoku against a person and shirt folding.
Figure 11:RoboDojo episodes:two tasks of each dimension, solved by SOLVE with GPT-6.1 Sol. Six head-camera keyframes per episode, each with the model call that sees it.

Figure 12:RoboLab episodes:ten tasks, labeled with one of their RoboLab attributes, solved by SOLVE with GPT-6.1 Sol. Six viewport keyframes per episode, at the model calls shown and at the end of the episode.

Figure 13:RoboTwin 2.0 episodesin the Easy setting, solved by SOLVE with GPT-6.1 Sol. Six head-camera keyframes per episode, each showing the observation seen at the indicated model call, so the last frame precedes the final motion.
